attrs.doc: Item text minus leading attributes, up to the body — signatures read `pub async fn f(...) -> T`, not `#[instrument] pub async fn f(...)`. Items without a body (`mod foo;`, trait method decls) sign in full.
The only thing that crosses the wire after handshake. Initial load is a chunked sequence of deltas bracketed by `Begin/EndSnapshot`; live updates are small deltas. One code path for both.
Relational vocabulary. `Contains`/`Defines` form the hierarchy tree (rendered as nesting, never force-layout); the rest cut across it (rendered as arcs).
Multiple edges of the same kind between the same pair (e.g. two call sites to one callee).
Compact runtime identity, interned per store. This is what appears on the wire and inside the client's normalized store.

Stable identity that survives edits and re-runs. The interner assigns `NodeId`s from `NodeKey`s; the key is what lets re-extraction after an edit recognize "same function, new body" and emit an upsert instead of remove+add.
Anonymous construct (call site, expression): anchored to the nearest stable ancestor + ordinal, so edits elsewhere in the file don't renumber the world.
Named definition. Survives body edits; a rename shows as remove+add unless the resolver patches it with rename tracking.

The server validates an intent against the legality table, compiles it to text edits via stored spans, applies them to files, and lets the re-parse delta flow back to all clients. Source files stay the single source of truth; the graph is always a derived view.
Edge-drag, e.g. fn→fn with kind=Calls inserts a call expression (plus an import if needed).
Drag-and-drop: move an item to another module/file.
Remove the construct that created the edge (a call, an import).
Applied to disk; the resulting delta arrives on the normal stream.
dry_run=true: edits ready for review.
A single text replacement, located via the node's stored provenance.
Same idea as LSP's WorkspaceEdit: the compiled, file-level result of an intent.
What the compiler thinks it's doing, for review UIs / agent confirmation.
Row/column, zero-based, matching tree-sitter's `Point`.
Source provenance for a node or edge. This is the layer that makes graph→code intents compilable into text edits, and cursor↔selection sync between graph and code pane.
Repo-relative path.

Monotonic store version. Every delta carries the version it was built against (`base_version`) and the version it produces (`version`), giving clients optimistic-concurrency detection and the server a way to reject stale edit intents instead of silently misapplying them.
An edge in the flattened snapshot.
A definition-level node in the flattened snapshot.
Short file path for display (e.g. `src/main.rs`).
The entire snapshot — everything the static visualizer needs.
All edges across all files.
Total files processed.
All definitions across all files, deduplicated by `NodeKey`.
Summary statistics.
Original tree-sitter node kind ("function_item", "call_expression").
Short display label (unqualified name).

The abstract, cross-language vocabulary the renderer thinks in. A few hundred tree-sitter grammar kinds collapse into this small set; the original grammar kind is preserved in `Node::ast_kind` for round-trip fidelity when compiling edit intents back to concrete syntax.
Synthetic anonymous node for a call site (uses an `Anchored` key).

A lens over the canonical store. The browser scene and the LLM text map are both projections under a ViewSpec; a lens is also a subscription filter on the delta stream, and `expand(node)` is how the LLM and the UI both implement semantic zoom.
Aggregate everything below this kind into weighted summary edges.
Path glob / predicate, kept as a string so the filter grammar can grow without protocol changes.
Zoomed-in subtree root; None = whole repo.
